takeaway: Hamstrings: semimembranosus, semitendinosus, biceps femoris. The short head of biceps femoris arises from the linea aspera.

question.text: Which of the following statements regarding the hamstring muscles is correct?

answer.text: The short head of biceps femoris originates from the linea aspera.

lines.text: The hamstrings are semimembranosus, semitendinosus and biceps femoris.
They mostly hang from the ischial tuberosity, the sitting bone, not the anterior superior iliac spine.
Semimembranosus runs to the medial condyle of the tibia, the inner side, not the lateral one.
Semitendinosus runs beside it and inserts deep to gracilis on the upper tibia.
Biceps femoris has two heads. The long head arises with semitendinosus.
But the short head starts lower down, on the femur.
It arises from the linea aspera, the rough ridge on the thigh bone.
So: short head of biceps from the linea aspera.
